Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: DPI Map confirms 'Enables authentication via government portal: YES'. In March 2020, Benin launched a standard platform for 300+ e-services using citizens' NPI for authentication. The eservices.anip.bj portal (37% of requests in 2025) and ANIP BJ mobile app (30%) use NPI-based authentication. Citizens can log in with their NPI to access official documents and services online.
revision_notes: Confirmed. DPI Map lists 'Authentication through government portal: YES'. February 2026 Biometric Update article confirms 37% of ANIP's 10.5 million identification/civil-status services were obtained through the digital government portal (eservices.anip.bj) in 2025, alongside the mobile app and USSD channels. Score 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Benin's National Agency for the Identification of Persons (ANIP) operates the eservices.anip.bj government portal and the ANIP BJ mobile app, enabling citizens to authenticate using their NPI and access official documents and services online. In 2025, 37% of the 10.5 million identification and civil-status services delivered were accessed through this digital government portal, alongside the mobile app (30%) and USSD (8%).

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Law 2017-08 Art. 48 gives individuals the right to obtain from ANIP the list of authorities that have accessed their data in the past 6 months. Law 2009-09 and the Digital Code (Law 2017-20) provide rights to access, rectify, and correct personal data. ANIP's platform (eservices.anip.bj) allows citizens to 'view and request modification of their data online'. The CNIB chip allows the cardholder to access their stored data.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ANIP's FAQ confirms citizens can 'consulter et... demander la modification de [leurs] données en ligne' via the eservices.anip.bj platform. ANIP's privacy policy (last updated 25 May 2025) sets out data subject rights. Official text of Law 2017-08 verified at sgg.gouv.bj (government legal-gazette portal) in place of the secondary ahjucaf.org copy. Score 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Under Law 2017-08 and the Digital Code (Law 2017-20), individuals have rights to access, rectify and correct their personal data. ANIP's eservices.anip.bj platform and mobile app allow citizens to view and request modification of their data online, and ANIP's privacy policy, updated in May 2025, documents these data subject rights.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: General judicial oversight exists through Benin's administrative courts (Law 2009-09 Art. 40 allows administrative court recourse against CNIL/APDP decisions). Law 2017-20 provides dispute resolution mechanisms. However, no specific ID-dedicated judicial oversight mechanism has been identified. The DPI Map notes a 'customer service mechanism' for redress rather than a legally binding judicial mechanism specific to ID.
revision_notes: Confirmed. APDP's own presentation states that 'les décisions de l'APDP peuvent faire l'objet de recours devant la juridiction administrative compétente', confirming general administrative-court oversight of data-protection/ID-related decisions rather than an ID-specific judicial mechanism. DPI Map lists only a customer-service redress mechanism, not a legally binding one. Score 2 (Yes, but not specific to ID) upheld.
revised_comments: General judicial oversight of ID-related administrative decisions exists through Benin's administrative courts: decisions of the data protection authority (APDP), which also oversees ID data processing, can be appealed to the competent administrative jurisdiction. No dedicated, ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism has been established; redress at the ID authority level is instead handled through a customer-service mechanism.

revised_comments: Rules governing the collection, storage and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available. ANIP publishes a detailed privacy policy, last updated in May 2025, covering its eservices.anip.bj platform and mobile app, and the Digital Code (Law 2017-20) sets out the purposes, categories of recipients and conditions for data sharing, overseen by the data protection authority (APDP).

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Law 2017-08 of June 19, 2017 specifically governs the identification of natural persons and the digital ID system in Benin. It establishes the NPI unique identifier, biometric data collection, the RNPP, and creates ANIP. The DPI Map confirms 'Regulation for digital ID: YES'. A dedicated legal and regulatory framework workshop was held in 2025 (WURI-organized) to further strengthen the electronic identification legal framework.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Official text of Law No. 2017-08 of 19 June 2017 (portant identification des personnes physiques) verified via the government's official legal-gazette portal (sgg.gouv.bj), establishing the NPI, biometric enrolment and ANIP. DPI Map confirms 'Regulation for digital ID: YES'. Score 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Law No. 2017-08 of 19 June 2017 specifically governs the identification of natural persons and digital identity in Benin, establishing the unique personal identification number (NPI), biometric data collection, the national population register, and the National Agency for the Identification of Persons (ANIP).

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Benin has two data protection laws: Law 2009-09 of May 22, 2009 on protection of personally identifiable information, and the more comprehensive Law 2017-20 (Digital Code) of April 20, 2018 (amended by Law 2020-35 of January 6, 2021), which includes GDPR-inspired data protection provisions. DPI Map confirms 'National Data Protection Act exists: YES'.
revision_notes: Confirmed. DLA Piper confirms Benin's data-protection regime rests on Law No. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018 (Digital Code), amended by Law No. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021, plus the earlier Law No. 2009-09 of 22 May 2009. The official amended Digital Code text was verified at haac.bj. Score 2 (Yes) upheld; year updated to reflect the most recent legislative amendment.
revised_comments: Benin has comprehensive data protection legislation covering personal data linked to the ID system: Law No. 2009-09 of 22 May 2009 on the protection of personal data, and Law No. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018 (the Digital Code), as amended by Law No. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021, which contains GDPR-inspired data protection provisions applicable to biometric identity data.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APDP) was established in Benin in 2018 under Article 462 of Law 2017-20, replacing the former CNIL. The APDP is an independent administrative body with legal personality. It supervises processing of personal data, investigates breaches, issues sanctions, and oversees compliance with the Digital Code, including for the biometric ID system.
revision_notes: Confirmed. APDP's own presentation confirms it is an independent administrative authority established under Law 2017-20, with powers of control and sanction over personal data processing, including biometric identity data. Score 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APDP), established under Law No. 2017-20 (replacing the earlier CNIL), is an independent administrative authority with legal personality that supervises personal data processing, investigates breaches and issues sanctions, including in respect of the biometric identification system.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The DPI Map confirms 'Identity act codifies legal status: YES'. Law 2017-08 establishes that the biometric national ID card and the NPI/fID certificate serve as legal proof of identity. Article 15 states every Beninese aged 18+ must hold the national biometric identity card. The fID certificate provides lifelong legal proof of identity for those lacking the full CNIB.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Official text of Law 2017-08 (verified at sgg.gouv.bj) establishes the identification of natural persons and legal status of the NPI/CNIB. World Bank (June 2024) confirms the fID/NPI certificate provides a 'lifelong... proof of identity'. DPI Map confirms 'Codified digital ID legal status: YES'. Score 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Law No. 2017-08 establishes that the biometric national identity card (CNIB) and the NPI/fID certificate serve as legal proof of identity in Benin. Every Beninese citizen aged 18 or over must hold the CNIB, while the fID certificate provides a lifelong, free proof of identity for residents who lack the full biometric card.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Benin has a comprehensive legal framework for digital ID. Law 2017-08 of June 19, 2017 establishes the identification of natural persons and creates ANIP. Decree 2018-206 of June 6, 2018 defines the organization of ANIP. Law 2017-20 (Digital Code) of April 20, 2018 governs digital services, e-signatures, data protection. Law 2009-09 established the earlier data protection framework (CNIL/APDP).
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law 2017-08 (verified at sgg.gouv.bj) establishes ANIP; ANIP's privacy policy cites Decree No. 2018-206 of 6 June 2018 on ANIP's organisation. The Digital Code (Law 2017-20) is confirmed via DLA Piper. Score 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Benin has a comprehensive legal framework for digital identity: Law No. 2017-08 of 19 June 2017 establishes the identification of natural persons and creates ANIP; Decree No. 2018-206 of 6 June 2018 defines ANIP's organisation; and Law No. 2017-20 (the Digital Code) of 20 April 2018 governs digital services, electronic signatures and data protection.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) issued Circular Note N 021/MEF/DC/USMEF/CTE/SP (January 8, 2021) requiring banks to accept ANIP biometric documents. ANIP receives state annual allocations via the finance law at the proposal of the Council of Ministers. ASIN (digital agency) is under dual supervision of the Ministry of Digital Technology and MEF. No direct full MoF oversight of ANIP but partial financial oversight exists.
revision_notes: Partially confirmed. The Ministry of Economy and Finance's circular note of 8 January 2021 shows the ministry actively regulates use of ANIP's biometric documents in the financial sector, and ANIP, like most public agencies, receives budget allocations via the annual finance law. No source was found confirming a dedicated MoF budget line or direct financial-oversight structure specific to ANIP/ID-system financing, so full oversight cannot be confirmed. Score 2 (Partial oversight) upheld but the direct evidence on financing oversight specifically remains thin; flagged for human review.
revised_comments: The Ministry of Economy and Finance exercises partial oversight of Benin's digital ID system: it regulates the acceptance of ANIP's biometric identity documents by financial institutions through a January 2021 circular note, and ANIP receives state funding through the annual finance law, though it does not have full, dedicated financial oversight of ANIP's budget and development.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Ministry of Economy and Finance Circular Note N 021/MEF/DC/USMEF/CTE/SP (January 8, 2021) mandates credit and microfinance institutions to accept ANIP biometric documents for banking formalities. The fID enables access to microcredit (e.g., Alafia program). 25 million eKYC verifications were completed in 2025. ID is accepted (and required for KYC compliance) but does not appear to be the only mandatory ID type for all banking - hence 'accepted not mandatory' for all banking types.
revision_notes: Confirmed. MEF circular note (8 Jan 2021) requires credit and microfinance institutions to accept ANIP's biometric identity documents (CNIB, biometric birth certificate, personal ID certificate) for banking formalities. February 2026 Biometric Update reports 25 million eKYC verifications completed via ANIP in 2025, indicating widespread but not exclusively mandatory use for financial services. Score 2 (Accepted but not mandatory) upheld.
revised_comments: ANIP's biometric identity documents are accepted for banking and financial-services formalities: a Ministry of Economy and Finance circular of January 2021 requires credit and microfinance institutions to accept them, and 25 million digital eKYC verifications using the ID system were completed in 2025. However, the ID is not established as the sole mandatory identity document for all banking purposes.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Law 2017-08 Art. 15 states every Beninese aged 18+ must hold the CNIB. A CNIB may be issued to a minor at the request of a parent/guardian. The fID/CNPI certificate is available from birth (newborns now receive a NPI at birth via the CRVS system). However, the mandatory CNIB eligibility age threshold is 18 (>17), qualifying as score 1.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Official text of Law 2017-08 (sgg.gouv.bj) establishes the CNIB as mandatory from age 18. The fID/NPI certificate can be obtained from birth via the digital civil-registration linkage, but the mandatory biometric-card eligibility threshold remains 18. Score 1 (>17) upheld; year corrected to 2017, the year the eligibility rule was legislated.
revised_comments: The National Biometric Identity Card (CNIB) becomes mandatory at age 18 under Law No. 2017-08. A card may be issued to a minor at a parent's or guardian's request, and the fID/NPI certificate is available from birth through the digital civil-registration system, but the standard eligibility age threshold for the credential is 18 (>17).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: CNIB is mandatory for all Beninese aged 18+ per Law 2017-08 Art. 15. However, the initial RAVIP enrollment campaign was voluntary ('not compulsory' per ID4Africa 2019 presentation). The fID/NPI certificate is voluntary for those who already have a CNIB. NPI is required to obtain any identity document and to access certain public services. Registration is mandatory for some but not uniformly for all categories including non-nationals.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law 2017-08 (sgg.gouv.bj) makes the CNIB mandatory for citizens 18+, while the 2019 ID4Africa presentation confirms the initial RAVIP biometric enrolment campaign was explicitly 'not compulsory'. Score 2 (Mandatory for some) upheld.
revised_comments: Registration for Benin's national ID is mandatory for some groups: the biometric national identity card (CNIB) is compulsory for citizens aged 18 and over under Law No. 2017-08, while the underlying RAVIP biometric enrolment campaign and the fID/NPI certificate for those already holding a CNIB remain voluntary.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: eID cards were handed to the poorest citizens specifically for free health services access (ID4Africa 2019 presentation). The ARCH health insurance program uses identity verification. ANIP's digital civil registration system is linked to health facilities for birth certificates. Social protection and health services are explicitly cited as use cases for the fID by World Bank. However, the ID does not appear to be universally mandatory for all healthcare access.
revision_notes: Mixed evidence. An official government source (gouv.bj) quotes the ANPS Director General stating that beneficiaries need to hold their biometric national ID card, issued by ANIP, to access care under the ARCH health-insurance scheme, suggesting the credential is effectively required (not merely accepted) within that flagship programme; ANPS's own site states health insurance 'will be made mandatory by law for all residents'. This is stronger than a plain 'Accepted but not mandatory' reading, but ARCH's health-insurance component does not yet cover all communes and general/emergency healthcare access outside ARCH does not appear to require the ID. Original score 2 retained rather than guessing an upgrade to 3 on partial evidence; flagged for human review to determine whether the ARCH requirement should move the score.
revised_comments: Benin's biometric national identity card, issued by ANIP, is used to access healthcare services under the ARCH social health-insurance programme: beneficiaries must hold the card to receive care, and free eID cards have also been distributed to the poorest citizens specifically to enable health-service access. The ID is not yet a universal requirement for all public healthcare access, as ARCH's health-insurance component is still being extended across all communes.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Law 2017-08 Art. 6 states that foreigners are included in the national biometric register when applying for residence cards (NPIR - Numéro Personnel d'Identification de Résident). The fID is available to 'all residents of Benin' per World Bank. MTN Benin SIM registration requires NPI for Beninese or NPIR for resident foreigners. The 2017 Identification Law introduced a unique identifier for foreign residents. Not all non-nationals are included (only residents/some categories), hence score 2.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law 2017-08 (sgg.gouv.bj) provides for a resident-foreigner identifier (NPIR) for foreigners applying for residence cards. World Bank (2024) confirms the fID is available to 'all residents of Benin' and Beninese citizens abroad, but coverage of non-resident categories (e.g. asylum seekers without residence status) is not confirmed. Score 2 (Some) upheld.
revised_comments: Non-nationals resident in Benin are eligible to register for the digital ID system: Law No. 2017-08 provides for a resident-foreigner identification number (NPIR) issued alongside residence cards, and the World Bank confirms the foundational identity (fID) system is open to all residents of Benin, though eligibility for undocumented or non-resident foreign categories is not established.
